obligation: DFARS 252.204-7012 Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting
basis: The clause is in the current DoD prime contracts and subcontracts with Prime A to Prime D, and the company holds covered defense information (controlled technical information) in the CEE, the MOZ and the KS-1 legacy environment. No size exemption. It applies to every covered contractor information system, including KS-1, and flows down to the 380 suppliers that receive CUI

obligation: CMMC Program rule (32 CFR Part 170) and DFARS 252.204-7021
basis: Contracts and subcontracts awarded from 2025-11-10 include DFARS 252.204-7021, most at Level 2 (C3PAO). The company holds Final Level 2 (C3PAO) for the CMMC Assessment Scope 'CEE and MOZ', CMMC Status Date 2026-03-20, with the annual affirmation due 2027-03-20 (32 CFR 170.22). As a prime it flows down CMMC requirements and confirms supplier status (252.204-7021(f); 32 CFR 170.23). No size exemption. Level 3 readiness is analyzed in P03

obligation: DFARS 252.204-7019 and 252.204-7020 NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment (SPRS)
basis: Both clauses are in the current contracts. SPRS holds two entries: the CEE and MOZ CAGE codes (110, from the 2026-03 certification assessment) and the KS-1 CAGE code (72, self-assessment dated 2025-01-28)

obligation: FAR 52.204-21 Basic Safeguarding of Covered Contractor Information Systems
basis: The clause is in the current contracts, and federal contract information sits in the ERP and corporate systems. Not a COTS-only acquisition

obligation: ITAR
basis: Registered with DDTC (22 CFR 122.1); military part data in PLM is ITAR technical data; release to a foreign person is an export (22 CFR 120.56)

obligation: EAR
basis: Commercial programs carry EAR-controlled technology; about 90 foreign-person employees work under deemed-export licenses or with technology that needs no license (15 CFR 734.13(a)(2))

obligation: NISPOM
basis: FL-1 holds a facility clearance for the Program K classified subcontract, with a stand-alone classified system authorized by DCSA and an FSO, ITPSO and ISSM appointed. Only cyber-relevant duties are analyzed. DCSA has not found the company to be under foreign ownership, control, or influence (32 CFR 117.11)

obligation: CUI program: safeguarding of CUI Basic
basis: Controlled technical information is CUI Basic and must be protected at no less than moderate confidentiality (2002.14(a)(3)); the duty reaches the company through its contracts

obligation: FAR 52.204-25 Covered telecommunications and video surveillance equipment
basis: The clause is in the current contracts; a report is due if covered equipment is found. The enterprise inventory was reviewed in 2026-03; KS-1 equipment was not

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incidents)
basis: Publicly traded SEC registrant, not a smaller reporting company. Confirmed in counsel's memo

obligation: SEC Regulation S-K Item 106 (risk management, strategy and governance)
basis: Same registrant status; the FY2025 Form 10-K includes Item 1C

obligation: Internal control over financial reporting (IT general controls)
basis: SEC registrant; ERP IT general controls are tested annually by the SOX program and not repeated in the gap analysis

obligation: State breach notification and data security laws
citation: Each state where affected individuals reside
basis: Employee personal information for staff in 6 states plus remote staff; the law of each state where affected individuals reside applies

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act (worked example)
basis: Headquarters, three plants and DC-1 are in Florida, so the company holds personal information of Florida residents

obligation: Sanctions check before any extortion payment
basis: Applies to all U.S. persons; payment needs CEO, General Counsel and insurer approval

obligation: Prime contract and subcontract notice terms
basis: Prime notice terms sit alongside the DFARS reporting duties; the incident report number goes to each higher-tier contractor

obligation: SL-1 and SL-2 customer agreements
basis: SL-1 turnaround and availability commitments to about 140 customers; SL-2 availability commitments to 19 operators, whose vendor programs ask for a SOC 2 report with Processing Integrity

obligation: Cyber insurance policy notice terms
basis: Notice to the carrier under the policy terms

obligation: Federal equal employment opportunity law applied to AI hiring tools
basis: The company is an employer with 12,000 employees, and the HR SaaS has a resume ranking feature switched on

obligation: Texas law on AI systems deployed with intent to discriminate
basis: The company hires in Texas at TX-1 and uses an AI resume screening feature

obligation: Colorado SB26-189 and similar state AI laws
basis: No operations in those states; counsel reviews each new state before hiring there

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reporting
basis: Final rule not published; counsel's memo lists it as pending

obligation: FAR CUI rule
basis: Not final; DFARS 252.204-7012 remains the governing clause

obligation: NIST SP 800-171 Rev. 3
basis: CMMC Level 2 is fixed to Rev. 2 (32 CFR 170.14(c)(3)); Rev. 3 is used for planning only

obligation: FedRAMP authorization as a cloud service provider
basis: The company sells no cloud services to the Government

obligation: HIPAA Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules
basis: The company is not a covered entity or business associate; employee benefits data is handled by the benefits program

obligation: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
basis: No consumer payment card acceptance; customers pay by invoice
